description: GPU architecture capability matrix.  Each entry is the MINIMUM set of features a GPU must have for an engine's kernels to compile (or to dispatch correctly).  Used to decide which arch-specific code paths to add.

fields.name: Human-readable arch name
fields.cpu: bool: true if this is a CPU arch entry (not a GPU)
fields.gpu: bool: true if this is a combined CPU+GPU APU entry
fields.wave_size: Wavefront/warp size (32 for NVIDIA, 32/64 for AMD RDNA/CDNA, 32 for Intel, 4 for NEON/SVE, 2 for x86 SSE)
fields.lds_kib: Local data share / shared memory per CU (0 for CPU-only arches)
fields.tensor_cores: bool: GPU matrix cores / MMA units
fields.features: dict of SIMD/ISA features for CPU entries (sse2, avx2, avx512, amx, neon, sve, sve2, aes, sha, fma3, apx, fp16_native)

gfx1201.name: RDNA4 (RX 9070 / 9070 XT / AI PRO R9700)

measured.provenance: RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), Windows, measured on-device; see PORTING-LESSONS.md sections 9, 12, 13
measured.runtime_unit_note: the runtime multiprocessor count returns workgroup processors (WGP), not compute units: 32 WGP = 64 CU

wmma_probed.note: ISA-verified by compiling and disassembling the unwrapped code object, not from a table
wmma_probed.spelling: gfx12 uses its own builtins with a _gfx12 suffix, eg __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu4_w32_gfx12; gfx11 spellings and raw asm with gfx11 operand shapes are rejected
wmma_probed.operand_shape: iu4 16x16x16 takes one scalar int per lane (8 nibbles); iu4 16x16x32 takes a 2-wide int vector; iu8 16x16x16 takes a 2-wide int vector; f16/bf16 take a 4-wide vector; the accumulator is always 8 registers
wmma_probed.builtin_signature: integer matrix builtins take (A_sign, A, B_sign, B, C, clamp); confirmed from the compiler's own gfx12 CodeGenHIP test in the vendor source tree, not inferred from the manual
wmma_probed.modifiers: neg_lo:[A,B,C] carries the per-operand sign interpretation plus a trailing clamp flag; real signed-int8 tuned code emits 'neg_lo:[1,1,0] clamp'
wmma_probed.tuned_census: across the whole tuned GEMM set for this target: MatrixInstruction is always [16,16,16,1], MacroTile 128x128 is most common (then 64x64), DepthU is 32 or 64, and there is no 4-bit kernel in the set
wmma_probed.tuned_inner_loop: a real tuned int8 kernel marshals operands with a byte permute (V_PERM_B32) and a half-word shared-memory load (DS_LOAD_U16_D16 / _HI), pipelines with S_WAIT_LOADCNT, uses S_BARRIER_SIGNAL in the loop, and the compiler emits dual-issued pairs (V_DUAL_MOV_B32) in the same block
wmma_probed.operand_expansion: narrow packed weights can be widened to 4-bit operands in registers with a byte permute, so no expanded weight copy needs to exist in device memory: this is the difference between losing the context to the weight expansion and keeping it
wmma_probed.dtype_pairs: gfx12 matrix pairs, all same-type: fp16/fp16, bf16/bf16, int8/int8 -> int32, and fp8/bf8 in all four mixes, all at K=16; plus packed-int4/packed-int4 -> int32 at K=16 and K=32. There is no mixed fp16xint4 pair on gfx12, so an int4 weight operand forces an int4 activation operand. fp4, fp6 and mixed fp16xint4 exist only on the gfx1250 family
wmma_probed.int4_packing: the packed 4-bit operand type is two int4 per byte with the low nibble first, and a compile-time variant swaps the nibble order
wmma_probed.generator_gap: the assembly-generating path behind the vendor BLAS library does have 4-bit datatypes, but only 4-bit FLOAT, plus a packed 4xint8 dword type that is used for dot products and is not a 4-bit integer. Its 4-bit-float matrix path is gated to the later gfx1250 family, and this target's matrix instruction set has no 4-bit float opcode at all, so no 4-bit kernel is generatable from its solution yaml for this target. It has no 4-bit integer datatype for any target. The 4-bit integer matrix path lives instead in the vendor's kernel-template library, which does expose it for this target at K=16 and K=32. Practical rule: presence of a datatype in the generator's enum is not availability on your target, because the matrix opcode behind it is capability-gated per ISA
wmma_probed.fp8: exists only as WMMA; no scalar fp8 conversion (v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32 is rejected)
wmma_probed.pipeline_rules: ISA 7.12.1 needs >=1 independent VALU between WMMAs whose operands overlap the previous D; 7.12.2 fixes lane/vgpr/startPosn per element; 11.6.2 gives GLOBAL_LOAD_TR_B64/B128 load-and-transpose straight into operand registers
wmma_probed.measured: dense matrix throughput measured with independent accumulator chains and round-robin interleaved rounds: int4 16x16x16 = 161 TOPS, int4 16x16x32 = 336 TOPS, fp16 16x16x16 = 179 TFLOPS. Both int4 forms peak at about 0.22 matrix instructions per CU per cycle, i.e. roughly one per 4.6 cycles and not one per cycle, so any figure derived from one-per-cycle is about 4.5x too high. The 16x16x32 form is 2.08x the 16x16x16 form at the same instruction rate, so the wider-K form is the one to use. fp16 is 3.7x the scalar FP32 vector rate and needs no activation quantisation, but the int4 K=32 form is 3.75x the fp16 MAC rate, so the choice trades numerical transparency against throughput. An earlier figure of 176 TOPS was not reproducible: its MAC count missed the number of matrix ops in the loop body, and its sequential sweep let the clock drift between variants

operand_width_vs_density.rule: for a memory-bound quantised matmul no wider operand can win at T=1 (dp4a 8 bits, fp8 8, iu4 4, fp16 16 against 2 packed); at batch T>=64 the weight read is amortised and compute binds instead, so matrix cores win

context_budget.rule: context tokens = free_bytes / per_token_bytes, so on this model 1 GB of device memory is about 30000 tokens and the whole context question reduces to which byte is a weight, which is a scratch buffer and which is K/V
context_budget.operand_expansion_cost: widening the packed weights to 4-bit in device memory would cost about 6.8 GB, i.e. roughly 193000 tokens of context, which is larger than the entire context currently in use, while the same widening done in registers costs no device memory at all
context_budget.sharding: splitting weights and K/V over two devices halves both per-device, so it raises the per-device context by roughly 2.5x and also halves the bytes each device must read per token

context_and_precision_ablation.method: effect on the next-token logits at one teacher-forced position after a 1024-token prompt, not greedy token streams, because free-running decode is chaotic and any perturbation diverges
context_and_precision_ablation.control: a window equal to the prompt length is a no-op and measured exactly 0.000, which validates the harness
context_and_precision_ablation.sliding_window: capping attention to the last W keys moves the logits by max 4.0 at W=256 and 10.1 at W=64 (argmax unchanged) and breaks the argmax at W=8, so context beyond the window is genuinely used and a sliding window is not free. The model is a hybrid whose 48 of 64 layers are linear attention with constant state, so this is the surface where one would have expected long range to live elsewhere; it does not
context_and_precision_ablation.kv_precision: re-quantising the q8_0 cache in place to 6 bits moves the logits by max 0.111 and to 4 bits by max 0.427, argmax unchanged at both, so a 4-bit cache is numerically far cheaper than any useful window and buys 1.9x the context
context_and_precision_ablation.pack_duplication: hashing every tensor blob in the 2-bit pack found 0 byte-identical tensors, so weight-content dedup recovers nothing; the pack is 17.2 GB of which 10.4 GB is a stale five-trit repack cache unused whenever the 2-bit path is selected

known_issues: no 4-bit matrix-core kernel ships for this target: the tuned BLAS solution set has none, and its generator cannot express a 4-bit datatype at all, so a 4-bit path has to be hand-written. The vendor's kernel-template library does expose packed-int4 at K=16 and K=32

matrix-core datatypes are same-type only here (fp16, bf16, int8, fp8 in all four mixes, packed int4): there is no narrow-weight/wide-activation pair, so choosing a 4-bit weight operand forces a 4-bit activation operand, which is a numerical change to whatever the activations feed
4-bit float exists in the generator but its opcode is gated to a later target family and is absent from this instruction set

measured on this target: int4 16x16x16 = 161 TOPS, int4 16x16x32 = 336 TOPS, fp16 16x16x16 = 179 TFLOPS, and both int4 forms issue about 0.22 matrix ops per CU per cycle rather than one, so any figure derived from one-per-cycle is roughly 4.5x too high

vulkan.notes: No WMMA/rocWMMA. Vulkan matmul must use DP4a-style SPIR-V.; Vulkan GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix broken on AMD — use DP4a

meteor_lake_iGPU.name: Meteor Lake iGPU (Intel Core Ultra 135H/155H, 8 CU Xe-LP)

arc_a770.name: Intel Arc A770 (Alchemist, 32 CU)
arc_a770.best_for: LLM inference (Q4_0/Q5_1), FP16/BF16 GEMM, Vulkan compute with DP4a or CooperativeMatrix (supported on Intel drivers)
arc_a770.not_for: FP8 workloads (no native FP8 on Alchemist)

uhd_gen12.name: Intel UHD Graphics Gen12 (10th-14th Gen Intel iGPU, 1-2 CU)
uhd_gen12.best_for: light Vulkan compute, OpenVINO CPU inference (not GPU)
uhd_gen12.not_for: LLM inference, GEMM, any serious compute

gen12_hp.name: Intel GEN12_HPC (Arc B-series Battlemage, Arc Pro B-series)
known_issues: Battlemage (B580, 24 CU): 512 GB/s GDDR6 — viable for LLM inference
FP8 native on Battlemage (check ISA docs for exact FP8 support)
Battlemage is GEN12_HPC-class — not the same as Arc A-series (GEN12_LP)

arc_b580.name: Intel Arc B580 (Battlemage, 24 CU)
arc_b580.best_for: LLM inference (Q4_0/Q5_1, FP8 if supported), BF16 GEMM via DPAS, Vulkan compute
arc_b580.not_for: FP16-only paths that don't use DPAS (DPAS is the matrix path)

gen12_hpc_battlemage.name: Intel Arc B580 (Battlemage, GEN12_HPC)
known_issues: DPAS is the matrix path (not WMMA)
FP8 native — verify exact FP8 datatype support in Battlemage ISA docs
Subgroup size 8 (EU subgroup of 8 threads) — different from AMD wave32, NVIDIA warp32
Battlemage is discrete Arc B-series — not an iGPU
oneAPI DPC++/SYCL is the primary compute path; Vulkan and DirectX 12 also supported

vulkan.notes: Intel drivers support GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix (unlike AMD). Use DPAS via SYCL for best matrix perf.; Vulkan CM supported on Intel drivers

meteor_lake.name: Intel Core Ultra (Meteor Lake) iGPU + hybrid CPU (Xe-LPG)
meteor_lake.measurement_source: kindi Vulkan port device dump on Core Ultra 5 135H (PORTING-DEEP-DIVE.md 2026-10-28); supersedes assumed values
meteor_lake.wave_size_note: driver reports min subgroup 8; pin 32 via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control or subgroup reductions silently corrupt (kindi measured)
meteor_lake.lds_kib_note: maxComputeSharedMemorySize=49152 measured; larger assumed values are wrong
meteor_lake.dot4_note: shaderIntegerDotProduct=1 but 4x8BitPackedSignedAccelerated=0 and 4x8BitPackedUnsignedAccelerated=0 — OpSDotKHR SCALARIZES; do not select packed-int8 idot4 paths (capability-ladder veto, kindi measured slower)
meteor_lake.memory_bandwidth_note: sustained shared-DDR5 fabric ceiling measured 37 GB/s via bwtest; scalar == 16B-vector == 8-chain loads plateau identically => true ceiling, not outstanding-loads limit (kindi measured)

cpu_side.topology: Core Ultra 5 135H: 4 P-cores + 8 E-cores + 2 LP-E, 18 threads
cpu_side.isa: AVX2 + FMA + AVX-VNNI(256-bit); AVX-512 fused off on retail MTL
cpu_side.implication: vnpu/AVX-512 VNNI GEMM paths never fire; INT8 loses to F32 without dpbusd — same feature-present-not-accelerated veto as the GPU dot4

known_issues: Integrated GPU shares system memory bandwidth — 37 GB/s measured ceiling, thermal throttling swings +-25%
No dedicated VRAM — performance depends on DDR5 speed
Driver hands out 8-lane subgroups unless pinned to 32 via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control — silently corrupts reductions
OpSDotKHR scalarizes (4x8BitPacked*Accelerated=0) — float FMA paths win
Use DPAS via oneAPI DPC++ (SYCL) if available; Vulkan compute should stick to float FMA
Power/thermal constraints on laptop APUs — measure ratios in same thermal window, not absolutes

vulkan.notes: Vulkan CooperativeMatrix requires Mesa 24.3+; on Windows Intel driver prefer plain float-FMA compute shaders; verify subgroupSize pinned at 32

gfx1031.name: AMD RDNA 3.5 (gfx1031)
gfx1031.notes: gfx1031 is RDNA 3.5 — same generation as gfx1150 family. No WMMA. Native BF16 + dot4. CDNA sibling: cdna3.

cdna2.name: AMD CDNA 2 (MI200)
cdna2.notes: CDNA 2 is AMD data-center ISA. Treat as RDNA2 compute sibling. WMMA + dot4 + BF16 native.

cdna3.name: AMD CDNA 3 (MI300)
cdna3.notes: CDNA 3 is AMD data-center ISA. RDNA3 compute sibling with fp8. WMMA + dot4 + BF16 + fp8 native.

zen3.name: AMD Zen 3 (Ryzen 5000 series, Vermeer)
zen3.notes: Zen 3 is AMD's 2020 desktop CPU. No AVX-512 (AMD dropped it on Zen 2/Zen 3). No AMX (AMX is Zen 4+). Good hipcc host (Clang 12+ under ROCm 6+). GCC 11+ recommended. 64-bit only. Not a GPU — CPU host for HIP/ROCm or CPU kernel path.

porting_notes.hipcc_host: ROCm hipcc works on Zen 3. Use Clang++ from ROCm's LLVM. GCC 11+ for native GCC builds.
porting_notes.cpu_kernel_path: If CPU kernel uses AVX-512 or AMX, rewrite for AVX2 + FMA3. Use -march=znver3 for GCC.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Zen 3 as CUDA host on Linux: GCC 11+ or Clang 12+. No AVX-512 issues (CUDA host code doesn't typically use AVX-512).
porting_notes.windows_cuda: Zen 3 + Windows needs MSVC — AMD CPU doesn't matter for Windows CUDA host (MSVC version matters, not CPU vendor).

intel_10th.name: Intel 10th Gen (Comet Lake, 14nm)
intel_10th.notes: Intel 10th Gen (Comet Lake, 14nm) — i9-10900K, i7-10700K, i5-10400. Has AVX-512. No AMX (AMX is 12th Gen+). iGPU is Gen12 LP UHD (not a compute target). Good CUDA host on Windows (MSVC 2019 v142). Good oneAPI host on Linux (GCC 10+).

porting_notes.cuda_host_windows: MSVC 2019 (v142) for CUDA 11.x. Intel CPU works as CUDA host — CPU vendor doesn't matter.
porting_notes.oneapi_host_linux: GCC 10+ for oneAPI DPC++ on Linux. Intel CPU is the natural host for oneAPI.
porting_notes.avx512_cpu_kernel: If CPU kernel uses AVX-512, it works on 10th Gen. But 12th-14th Gen Intel disables AVX-512 — if targeting 12th+ Gen, rewrite for AVX2.
porting_notes.igpu_compute: Gen12 LP UHD iGPU (1-2 CU) is NOT a real compute target. No DPAS. Use OpenVINO CPU inference or Vulkan light compute only.

intel_11th.name: Intel 11th Gen (Rocket Lake, 14nm)
intel_11th.notes: Intel 11th Gen (Rocket Lake, 14nm) — i9-11900K, i7-11700K, i5-11600K. Has AVX-512. No AMX. iGPU is Gen12 UHD (similar to 10th Gen — not a compute target). Good CUDA host on Windows (MSVC 2019 v142).

porting_notes.oneapi_host_linux: GCC 11+ for oneAPI DPC++ on Linux.
porting_notes.avx512_cpu_kernel: AVX-512 available. Same caveats as 10th Gen — disable on 12th+.
porting_notes.igpu_compute: Gen12 UHD iGPU — not a compute target.

intel_12th.name: Intel 12th Gen (Alder Lake, 10nm + 14nm hybrid)
intel_12th.notes: Intel 12th Gen (Alder Lake, hybrid P-core + E-core) — i9-12900K, i7-12700K, i5-12600K. AVX-512 DISABLED (Intel disabled AVX-512 on hybrid arch). No AMX. iGPU is Gen12 UHD (not a compute target). Good CUDA host on Windows (MSVC 2022 v143). Hybrid CPU: use taskset or CMake to pin to P-cores for performance.

porting_notes.cuda_host_windows: MSVC 2022 (v143) for CUDA 12.x. Intel CPU works as CUDA host.
porting_notes.oneapi_host_linux: GCC 12+ for oneAPI DPC++ on Linux.
porting_notes.avx512_disabled: AVX-512 is NOT available on 12th Gen. If CPU kernel uses AVX-512, rewrite for AVX2. This is the first Intel gen where AVX-512 is gone.
porting_notes.hybrid_cpu: P-cores + E-cores. Pin performance-critical CPU kernel paths to P-cores (taskset or CMake). E-cores have lower IPC and no AVX-512.
porting_notes.igpu_compute: Gen12 UHD iGPU (or Arc graphics on some SKUs) — UHD is not a compute target. If the SKU has Arc graphics, it's a discrete-ish GPU (still on the motherboard) — check if it's GEN12_LP (Arc A-series class) or better.

intel_13th.name: Intel 13th Gen (Raptor Lake, 10nm + 14nm hybrid)
intel_13th.notes: Intel 13th Gen (Raptor Lake, hybrid) — i9-13900K, i7-13700K, i5-13600K. AVX-512 DISABLED. No AMX. iGPU is Gen12 UHD (not a compute target). Good CUDA host on Windows (MSVC 2022 v143). Hybrid CPU — pin to P-cores. Note: 13th/14th Gen i9 instability issues (Vmin shift) — be aware if running sustained GPU compute workloads that stress CPU power delivery.

porting_notes.oneapi_host_linux: GCC 12+ for oneAPI DPC++ on Linux.
porting_notes.avx512_disabled: AVX-512 not available. Same as 12th Gen.
porting_notes.hybrid_cpu: P-cores + E-cores. Pin to P-cores for CPU kernel perf.
porting_notes.cpu_instability: 13th/14th Gen i9 instability (Vmin shift) — sustained high-load workloads may trigger instability. Monitor CPU temps/power if running long GPU compute jobs that also stress the CPU power delivery.
porting_notes.igpu_compute: Gen12 UHD iGPU — not a compute target. Meteor Lake iGPU (Intel Core Ultra) is the first Intel iGPU worth computing on.

intel_14th.name: Intel 14th Gen (Raptor Lake Refresh, 10nm + 14nm hybrid)
intel_14th.notes: Intel 14th Gen (Raptor Lake Refresh, hybrid) — i9-14900K, i7-14700K, i5-14600K. AVX-512 DISABLED. No AMX. iGPU is Gen12 UHD (not a compute target). Good CUDA host on Windows (MSVC 2022 v143). Same as 13th Gen with minor clock bumps. Same instability caveats for i9.

porting_notes.oneapi_host_linux: GCC 13+ for oneAPI DPC++ on Linux.
porting_notes.avx512_disabled: AVX-512 not available. Same as 12th/13th Gen.
porting_notes.cpu_instability: Same 13th/14th Gen i9 instability caveats. Monitor temps/power for sustained workloads.
porting_notes.igpu_compute: Gen12 UHD iGPU — not a compute target. Meteor Lake (Intel Core Ultra) is the first Intel iGPU worth computing on.

strix_point.name: AMD Strix Point APU (Ryzen AI 9 365, RDNA 3 iGPU gfx1100-class)
strix_point.notes: Strix Point is AMD's 2024-2025 laptop APU (Zen 4 CPU + RDNA 3 iGPU, gfx1100-class). 12 CUs RDNA 3 iGPU. Shares DDR5/LPDDR5X system memory. WMMA available on the iGPU (gfx1100-class). HIP/ROCm supports gfx1100 iGPU. Best for laptop LLM inference (7B-13B models) where power/thermal matters. Not for server-class workloads.

porting_notes.hipcc_target: Use hipcc --offload-arch=gfx1100 for Strix Point iGPU. Same as discrete RDNA 3 gfx1100 target.
porting_notes.wmma_available: WMMA fp16 path available on Strix Point iGPU (gfx1100-class). Same as discrete RX 7900 XT WMMA path.
porting_notes.shared_memory: DDR5/LPDDR5X shared memory — ~72-128 GB/s bandwidth. Bottleneck for large models. Not for models that don't fit in iGPU memory.
porting_notes.cpu_path: Zen 4 CPU (Strix Point CPU) — has AVX-512? No, Zen 4 has AVX-512 but it's been disabled on some APU configs. Check specific APU — Strix Point may have AVX-512 enabled or disabled depending on the SKU.
porting_notes.use_case: Laptop LLM inference (7B-13B quantized). Power/thermal constrained (laptop). Not for high-throughput serving.

strix_halos.name: AMD Strix Halo APU (Radeon 8060S, RDNA 3.5 iGPU gfx1150-class, 40 CU rumored)
strix_halos.notes: Strix Halo is AMD's upcoming 2025 laptop APU (Zen 5 CPU + RDNA 3.5 iGPU, gfx1150-class, 40 CU rumored). RDNA 3.5 iGPU — same as gfx1150 feature set (WMMA, BF16 native, dot4, dot8). Shares DDR5/LPDDR5X system memory. Much higher CU count than Strix Point (40 CU vs 12 CU). HIP/ROCm supports gfx1150 iGPU. Best for laptop LLM inference with higher throughput than Strix Point.

porting_notes.hipcc_target: Use hipcc --offload-arch=gfx1151 for Strix Halo iGPU. Same as gfx1151 target (RDNA 3.5).
porting_notes.wmma_available: WMMA fp16 path available on Strix Halo iGPU (gfx1151-class). Same as gfx1150 WMMA path.
porting_notes.shared_memory: DDR5/LPDDR5X shared memory — higher bandwidth than Strix Point (more CUs, more memory channels rumored). Still a bottleneck vs discrete GPU (960 GB/s).
porting_notes.use_case: Higher-throughput laptop LLM inference than Strix Point. 40 CU iGPU can do more than 12 CU Strix Point. Still laptop power/thermal constrained.
porting_notes.status: Rumored/upcoming — verify exact CU count and feature set when hardware ships.

x86_64.name: x86-64 baseline (SSE2 minimum)
x86_64.notes: x86-64 baseline: SSE2 only. This is the minimum guarantee from the x86-64 spec. Any CPU claiming x86-64 support has SSE2. Use this for portability analysis: code that requires AVX2 or AVX-512 must fall back here.

porting_notes.compiler_flags: GCC/Clang: no -march= flag (SSE2 is baseline). MSVC: /arch:SSE2 (default).
porting_notes.fallback: Where AVX2/AVX-512 is unavailable, fall back to scalar C++ or SSE2 intrinsics.

zen4.name: AMD Zen 4 (Ryzen 7000 series, EPYC 9004 series)
zen4.notes: Zen 4 (2022) desktop/server CPU. First AMD consumer CPU with AVX-512 (Zen 4 reintroduced it, unlike Zen 2/Zen 3 which dropped it). No AMX (AMX is Intel-only). Supports V-Cache variants (7845HX3D, etc.). Good hipcc host (Clang 15+ under ROCm 5.7+). GCC 12+ or Clang 15+ recommended.

porting_notes.avx512: AVX-512 IS available on Zen 4 (unlike Zen 3). If CPU kernel uses AVX-512, it works here.
porting_notes.hipcc_host: ROCm hipcc works on Zen 4. Use Clang++ from ROCm's LLVM.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Zen 4 as CUDA host on Linux: GCC 12+ or Clang 15+. AVX-512 fully supported.
porting_notes.windows_cuda: Zen 4 + Windows needs MSVC 2022 (v143). AMD CPU is neutral for CUDA host.

zen5.name: AMD Zen 5 (Ryzen 9000 series, EPYC 9005 series)
zen5.notes: Zen 5 (2024) desktop/server CPU. AVX-512 retained (same as Zen 4). Adds APX (Advanced Performance Extensions) in some SKUs. No AMX. 16KB L1D (vs 32KB on Zen 4). Supports V-Cache (9800X3D). Good hipcc host (ROCm 6.2+). GCC 13+ or Clang 17+ recommended. FP64 throughput improved 2x vs Zen 4.

porting_notes.apx: APX adds 3-operand instructions for better code density. Requires GCC 14+ or Clang 18+.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Zen 5 as CUDA host: GCC 13+ or Clang 17+.
porting_notes.l1d_16k_warning: 16KB L1D (vs 32KB Zen4) — cache-sensitive kernels may need tuning.

apple_m2.name: Apple M2 (ARM64, 8-core CPU + 10-core GPU)
apple_m2.notes: Apple M2 (2023) ARM64 SoC. NEON SIMD (128-bit, 4-wide vector). No AVX/AVX-512 (ARM SIMD is fundamentally different). Hardware AES/SHA. Unified memory (shared LPDDR5). CPU is the primary porting concern: x86 code must be translated (Rosetta 2) or recompiled. Metal is the native GPU API; Vulkan via MoltenVK; CUDA not supported.

porting_notes.compiler_flags: Clang: -arch arm64 -mcpu=apple-m2. GCC: -arch arm64 -mcpu=native (via cross-compile on Linux).
porting_notes.avx_replacement: AVX2 (256-bit) → NEON (128-bit): need 2x iterations. AVX-512 (512-bit) → 4x NEON iterations. Use ACLE __builtin vectors or inline asm.
porting_notes.hipcc_host: Not supported (no ROCm on Linux ARM desktop). Use Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) instead.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Not supported on Apple Silicon. Use Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) / MoltenVK / Vulkan.
porting_notes.simd_width: NEON is 128-bit (4x float32 or 8x int16). Wave/warp analogy = 4 lanes for float32.

apple_m3.name: Apple M3 (ARM64, 8-core CPU + 10-core GPU, 3nm)
apple_m3.notes: Apple M3 (2023) ARM64 SoC, 3nm process. NEON SIMD. Native FP16 (unlike M1/M2 which required software emulation for some FP16 ops). Same caveats as M2 for x86 porting. No AVX. Best for on-device LLM inference (Metal + MLX framework).

porting_notes.fp16_native: M3 has hardware FP16 multiply-add (unlike M1/M2). Can use native bf16/fp16 kernels.
porting_notes.hipcc_host: Not supported. Use Apple MLX framework for LLM on Apple Silicon.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Not supported. Use Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) / MoltenVK / Vulkan.
porting_notes.avx_replacement: AVX → NEON via Apple's simd.h or ACLE intrinsics. For LLM inference, MLX framework provides optimized kernels.

apple_m4.name: Apple M4 (ARM64, 10-core CPU + 16-core GPU, 3nm+)
apple_m4.notes: Apple M4 (2024) ARM64 SoC, 3nm+ EUV process. 10-core CPU (6P + 4E). 16-core GPU. Native FP16. NEON SIMD. Supports ray tracing in GPU. First Apple Silicon with AV1 decode in hardware. MLX framework runs well.

porting_notes.hipcc_host: Not supported. Use Apple MLX framework.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Not supported. Use Metal / MoltenVK / Vulkan.
porting_notes.avx_replacement: AVX → NEON via Apple's simd.h or ACLE intrinsics.
porting_notes.best_for: On-device LLM inference via MLX (Qwen, Llama, etc.) with native GPU acceleration through Metal.

aarch64_neoverse.name: ARM Neoverse N3 / V2 / N2 (server ARM64)
aarch64_neoverse.notes: ARM Neoverse server CPU (N2/V2/N3, 2021-2025). SVE2 SIMD (up to 256-bit vector registers, runtime-determined length). NEON backward compatible. Native FP16. Runs Linux/llama.cpp efficiently. AWS Graviton3/Graviton4, Ampere Altra, AmpereOne use this class. No AVX. Good for native llama.cpp CPU inference on ARM servers.

porting_notes.sve2: SVE2 provides predication + 256-bit vectors. NEON (128-bit) is the minimum. Code must handle variable SVE vector length (VL) at runtime.
porting_notes.hipcc_host: Not supported natively. AMD ROCm supports aarch64 for AMD Instinct GPUs alongside Neoverse CPUs.
porting_notes.cuda_host: Not applicable. Use oneAPI DPC++ / OpenACC for offload, or CPU-native inference.
porting_notes.best_for: Server-class LLM CPU inference (llama.cpp, tinyvllm CPU backend). SVE2 provides good throughput for fp16/bf16 GEMM.
porting_notes.runtime_detection: Use getauxval(AT_HWCAP) to check for SVE2 at runtime. SVE VL varies by implementation.

gfx1031.name: AMD RDNA 3.5
gfx1031.notes: RDNA 3.5 class. Similar to gfx1030 but with improved LDS and some gfx1100 traits. Builds with gfx1030-targeted HIP; same portable kernel path. No WMMA, no fp8. BF16 native. Check gfx103x vs gfx1030 LDS sizing differences.

kernel_notes.moe: exl3 + native_moe compile;no WMMA MMQ path

cdna2.name: AMD CDNA 2
cdna2.notes: CDNA 2 is AMD data-center ISA (MI200). Closely related to RDNA compute but with matrix cores (WMMA) and no graphics pipeline. Treat as sibling to gfx1030 RDNA2 class. Use HIP toolchain targeting gfx90a.

kernel_notes.moe: exl3 + native_moe; MMQ path via gfx90a matrix cores

cdna3.name: AMD CDNA 3
cdna3.notes: CDNA 3 is AMD data-center ISA (MI300). Adds native fp8 support and improved matrix cores over CDNA 2. Treat as sibling to RDNA3 gfx1100 compute. Use HIP toolchain targeting gfx940/gfx941/gf942.

kernel_notes.attention: WMMA fp16 + fp8 matmul path available
kernel_notes.moe: exl3 + native_moe; fp8 MMQ path via gfx94x matrix cores
